meta.requirement: Explore Springvale (30%+ exploration) to trigger this quest.

customTabs.label: TIP
customTabs.content:
You can click the '''Collapse''' button and the '''Best Route''' → '''Important Only''' button at the top to minimize it.
''Some quests will not have a Best Route choice, because the best choice is subjective or not yet found.''

You can also click the '''Endings''' button at the top to view all possible endings, and clicking an ending will show the options needed to reach that ending.

start.title: Fred
start.text:
''He's sitting on the low fence at the edge of a field, facing away from the village, hands resting in his lap. Not watching anything. Not doing anything. Just sitting.''

''You almost walk past. Then he turns his head slightly at the sound of your steps, and you see his face. It isn't the face of someone resting.''

''It's the face of someone who has been very still for a very long time.''

Fred: ''quietly'' Oh. Hey.

choices.label: Are you alright?

Are_you_alright_.text:
Fred: ''a short pause'' Yeah. Yeah, I'm fine.

''He looks back at the field.''

Fred: Just getting some air.

''A beat.''

Fred: ...I've been getting a lot of air lately.

choices.label: How long have you been out here?

How_long_have_you_been_out_here_.text:
Fred: ''glances at the sky, as if that might give him the answer''

Fred: Since this morning, I think. Maybe before that.

''He exhales, slow and careful.''

Fred: I'm just... tired. Not sleepy. Just. ''he presses his thumb into his palm'' Tired all the way through. Every morning it's the same. Get up. Try. Come home. Try again. ''quietly'' I keep waiting for it to feel like something.

choices.label: What's at home?
How long has it been like this?

Whats_at_home.text:
Fred: ''without hesitation'' My wife. My kids. Two of them. ''small, tired smile that doesn't reach his eyes'' Good kids. Really good kids.

''He looks down at his hands.''

Fred: They deserve better than what I've been giving them lately. I know that. I do. ''quieter'' I just don't know how to be more than this right now.

''He doesn't say it plainly. He doesn't have to. Something in the way he says it carries the full weight of what he means.''

choices.label: Is there anything I can do?

Is_there_anything_I_can_do_.text:
Fred: ''looks at you properly for the first time, as if deciding whether you mean it''

Fred: ...Actually. ''shifts on the fence'' I was going to cook tonight. Something proper. I used to cook, back before things got like this. My wife always said I made too much food, but she'd eat three helpings and pretend otherwise.

''He almost smiles. Almost.''

Fred: I don't have the ingredients. I haven't been out far enough to get them. Mushroom, and some Fowl. ''quietly'' If you find any, I'd... I think I'd like to do one thing right today. ''a pause'' You could stay for it. If you wanted.

choices.label: I'll get them. Ten Mushroom, five Fowl.

I_ll_get_them__Ten_Mushroom__five_Fowl_.text:
Fred: ''a long moment, then he nods, just once''

Fred: Thank you. ''simply'' I'll be at the house. The one with the broken shutter on the left window. My wife keeps asking me to fix it.

''He pauses.''

Fred: I'll fix it. While you're out.

''He slides off the fence and walks back toward the village, a little more like a person than he was a moment ago. A little.''

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Gather 10 Mushroom and 5 Fowl and bring them to Fred in Springvale

continues.label: Do /rpg again and then click on Bring Fred the Ingredients

Bring_Fred_the_Ingredients.text:
''The shutter is fixed.''

''It's a small thing, but it's there. The latch is straight, the hinge is seated properly, and the whole frame sits square for probably the first time in years.''

''Fred opens the door before you knock. He looks at what you're carrying and something crosses his face.''

Fred: You actually got them.

choices.label: Ten Mushroom and five Fowl
Not quite yet. Still gathering

Not_quite_yet__Still_gathering.text:
Fred: ''nods, no frustration in it''

Fred: Right. ''steps back from the door'' I'll be here. ''almost adds something, then doesn't''

''He glances over his shoulder into the house. Somewhere inside, one of his kids laughs at something.''

Fred: ''quietly'' Take your time.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Gather 10 Mushroom and 5 Fowl and bring them to Fred in Springvale

Ten_Mushroom_and_five_Fowl.text:
''You hand everything over. Fred takes it carefully, as though the mushrooms and fowl are something more than mushrooms and fowl.''

Fred: Come in. ''steps back'' Please.

''The inside of the house is worn but tended. Boots lined up near the door. A drawing on the wall, clearly done by a small hand, of four figures holding hands. The name "Papa" is written above one of them in uneven letters.''

choices.label: It smells good in here

It_smells_good_in_here.text:
Fred: ''already at the counter, moving with a focus he didn't have out on that fence'' That's bread from this morning. My wife made it. ''reaches for a pan'' I used to cook when the kids were small. It settled me.

''He works quietly. The sound of children arguing about something small drifts from the back room. Fred doesn't look up, but his shoulders drop a fraction.''

''His wife appears in the doorway, a tired woman with a kind face. She sees you, sees the pan, sees Fred's hands moving. She doesn't say anything for a moment.''

Wife: ''softly'' You're cooking.

choices.label: He wanted to do something right today

He_wanted_to_do_something_right_today.text:
''She looks at you, then back at Fred. Something in her face shifts, careful and hopeful at once, like she doesn't want to startle whatever this is.''

Wife: ''to Fred, quietly'' Do you need anything?

Fred: ''doesn't look up from the pan'' Not right now. ''a beat'' Maybe just... come eat with us later.

''She stays in the doorway for a moment. Then she nods and goes back to the children.''

''Fred keeps cooking. You watch. Neither of you says anything, and neither of you needs to.''

choices.label: Just wait

Just_wait.text:
''Dinner is loud in the way dinners with small children always are. The kids talk over each other. Someone spills water and Fred cleans it up without raising his voice. His wife keeps stealing small glances at him, taking stock of something.''

''The food is good. Better than good. His daughter asks for seconds of the mushrooms, then thirds, and Fred almost laughs.''

''Then the children are in bed, and his wife says she'll clean up, and you end up on the front step with Fred as the village settles into evening. The shutter is still straight. The lane is quiet.''

Fred: ''after a long while'' You didn't have to do any of this.

choices.label: You asked

You_asked.text:
Fred: ''turns his cup slowly in both hands''

Fred: I've been thinking, lately. About how much easier it would be if I just... wasn't here anymore. Not for anyone to deal with. ''quietly, not dramatic, only tired'' My wife would be sad for a while. The kids would be confused. But they'd find their footing. They'd be okay eventually, I think. Better without me dragging around behind them.

''He says it the way people say things they have turned over so many times the edges have worn smooth.''

Fred: I know how it sounds. I'm not stupid. I just can't seem to stop thinking it.

choices.label: Your family doesn't need you gone. They need you here
What if this place isn't the right fit for you anymore?
...I don't know what to say to that

Your_family_doesn_t_need_you_gone__They_.text:
Fred: ''a long silence''

Fred: They'd be better off with someone who—

''He stops himself.''

''He sets his cup down on the step.''

Fred: You know what my daughter drew on the wall in there? ''quietly'' She drew four people. She put my name above the tall one.

''He stares at the ground.''

Fred: She still put my name on it.

choices.label: That tall figure isn't replaceable. Not to her

That_tall_figure_isn_t_replaceable__Not_.text:
Fred: ''his jaw tightens''

Fred: I'm not enough, though. That's the thing. I wake up every morning and I feel like a shape of a person. Like I'm going through motions someone else wrote for me.

''His voice drops.''

Fred: I don't even know who I am outside of all the things I'm supposed to be.

''He is very still.''

choices.label: That hollow feeling isn't permanent. But leaving is

That_hollow_feeling_isn_t_permanent__But.text:
''Fred doesn't answer right away.''

''Somewhere inside the house, one of his kids says something in their sleep. Audible through the cracked window. Fred tilts his head toward the sound, just slightly.''

Fred: ''very quietly'' I fixed the shutter today.

''A long pause.''

Fred: That's... I don't know. That's something, isn't it.

''He presses both hands flat against his knees. A decision moving through him.''

Fred: I'm not okay. I want you to know I know that. But I'm going to go inside now. ''exhales, uneven'' I'm going to go be with them.

choices.label: Go

Fred__Still_Here.title: Still Here
Fred__Still_Here.text:
''Fred stands, picks up both cups, and pauses at the door.''

Fred: I don't know your name. ''almost amused, almost sad'' You came to my house, helped me cook, sat at my table, and I don't know your name.

''He shakes his head.''

Fred: Thank you. ''simply'' I mean it. I don't know what tonight would have looked like without this.

''He goes inside. You hear, faintly, the creak of a chair. His wife's voice, low. Then quiet.''

''The shutter is still straight. The lane is still quiet. You stand there for a moment, then walk on.''

''Some things you don't need to see the end of. It's enough to know they continued.''

What_if_this_place_isn_t_the_right_fit_f.text:
Fred: ''blinks, like he expected something different''

Fred: What do you mean?

''He's still holding the cup, but his grip has loosened slightly.''

choices.label: You spend every day doing things for other people. When did you last do something for yourself?

You_spend_every_day_doing_things_for_oth.text:
Fred: ''opens his mouth. Closes it again.''

Fred: ...I used to go out to the field as a kid. Before all of this. Just to see what was past the treeline. ''pause'' I never went far. I always came back before dark. But I liked not knowing what was out there.

''He stares into his cup.''

Fred: I forgot I used to do that.

choices.label: The Adventurers' Guild is always looking for people

The_Adventurers__Guild_is_always_looking.text:
Fred: ''a short, surprised sound, not quite a laugh''

Fred: Me? An adventurer? ''looks at his hands'' I fix fences and burn the toast.

''But he hasn't said no.''

choices.label: Half the Guild started exactly like that
Everyone starts small. The first rank is just short jobs

Half_the_Guild_started_exactly_like_that.text:
''Fred is quiet for a long time. The village sounds have settled down to almost nothing now. A dog somewhere. Wind moving through the crops.''

Fred: ''slowly'' I can't just leave them.

Fred: ''then, to himself'' But I could take a short job. Come back. ''he seems to be working something out in real time'' It's not disappearing. It's just... go see what's past the treeline. Actually go this time.

''Something in his face is different. It isn't fixed. But it's awake.''

Fred: The guild's in Mondstadt City?

choices.label: Ask for the front counter. They'll sort you out

A_New_Path.title: A New Path
A_New_Path.text:
Fred: ''nods slowly, pressing the decision into place''

Fred: Okay. ''picks up his cup'' Okay.

''He stands and stretches. There is a straightness in his back that wasn't there on the fence this afternoon.''

Fred: I'm going to tell my wife tonight. ''then, with the first flicker of real humor all evening'' She'll probably say she already knew I'd figure this out eventually.

''He holds the door open.''

Fred: Thank you for dinner. ''quiet'' And the rest.

''Weeks later, word spreads through Springvale as word tends to. A man from the east lane registered with the Adventurers' Guild. Started with small jobs, slimes along the path mostly. He came home every time. His daughter drew a new picture on the wall: four figures at the house, and one smaller shape far off at the edge of the paper, standing alone with a sword.''

___I_don_t_know_what_to_say_to_that.text:
''You don't.''

''Fred nods, like that's exactly the answer he expected.''

Fred: That's alright. ''flatly'' Nobody does.

''He finishes his cup. Sets it carefully on the step beside him.''

Fred: You should probably head on. Getting late.

choices.label: ...I hope things get easier
Fred, wait. I want to try

I_hope_things_get_easier.text:
Fred: ''quiet, and not unkind''

Fred: It's okay.

''He stands and collects both cups with the careful, deliberate motion of someone who wants their hands occupied.''

Fred: I'm glad you came. I mean that. ''genuinely'' It was a good dinner.

''He holds the door open.''

Fred: Safe travels, traveller.

choices.label: Goodnight, Fred

____Fred__Too_Late.title: Too Late
____Fred__Too_Late.text:
''You walk back through Springvale alone.''

''Three days later you hear about it at the edge of a conversation you weren't meant to catch. A man from the east lane. A family. A morning when his wife found the bed empty and the back door open.''

''You never knew his surname. You don't learn it now.''

''The words you couldn't find on that step were still somewhere in your chest. They stayed there a long time after.''

Fred__wait__I_want_to_try.text:
Fred: ''stops. Looks at you.''

''You open your mouth. You have something to say. You just need to find it.''

''...''

''The words don't come.''

choices.label: ...I can't find the words
